problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{arccos}⁡y}{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.$*
worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le \operatorname{arccos}⁡y,\,\,0\le x\le 2}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/c5f4ec9b9b12411f3057bc074a14a1f541c768c30d3a9746d7a0484b0491ad2e.png)

The region $D$ is type I region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le z\le \operatorname{arccos}⁡y}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
y=0
$$

and the right boundary of the region $D,$ written in the form $y=y(z),$ is

$$
z=\operatorname{arccos}⁡y\,⟹\,y=\operatorname{cos}⁡z.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region is

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \operatorname{cos}⁡z},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/077fc8133673cd57aba570cca9a6e0f5f25aa742720948c46db2b9e1d05add69.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{arccos}⁡y}{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}[{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}y\,[x]_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}2y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}2y\,\text{d}y]\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{y}^{2}]_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{cos}^{2}⁡z\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\frac{1}{2}(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡2z)\,\text{d}z \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[z+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2z]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
